ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-expert output decorrelation during pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer, two active per token and 600 million active parameters on 30 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Add to the language modeling loss a term that penalizes cosine similarity between the mean outputs of experts on the tokens routed to both of them, with weight 0.01. Evaluate held-out perplexity in each language, the GSM8K mathematics set, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare with the same architecture trained with load balancing alone, same tokens and schedule. Compare with global-batch load balancing and with a router orthogonality regularizer. Run three seeds per configuration and report paired bootstrap intervals.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Expert overlap should fall and average downstream accuracy should rise by about one point over the load-balancing-only run, with perplexity unchanged. The effect would vanish if the decorrelation term only shifts which experts fire without changing what they compute.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-aligned routing prior from document sources
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 32 experts per layer and top-two routing on 50 billion tokens whose documents carry coarse source labels: English web, Chinese web, mathematics and encyclopedia text. Add an auxiliary loss that pulls the average router distribution of each source toward a distinct subset of experts, leaving routing free within the subset, and anneal its weight to zero over the final fifth of training. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, a broad exam-style knowledge benchmark and a reading comprehension suite, and measure how much of each expert's load comes from a single source. Compare with load balancing alone and with a version whose source labels are permuted across documents, using three seeds each.
CONTROLS: The reference runs are a load-balancing-only model on the same stream, a permuted-label version of the auxiliary loss at the same weight, and a global-batch load-balancing model. Each is repeated with three seeds, and differences are read from paired bootstrap intervals on every downstream score.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Source concentration per expert should rise clearly and downstream scores should improve a little over load balancing alone, while the permuted-label run should look like the plain reference. If the permuted-label run gains as much, the benefit comes from the extra regulariser and not from the source guidance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mutual-information routing loss for expert specialisation
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language modelling system with 24 experts per layer and two active per token, using 800 million active parameters and 40 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Cluster token representations from a small frozen model into 24 groups and add a loss that maximises the mutual information between the cluster and the chosen expert, with weight 0.02. Evaluate perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and analyse how concentrated each expert's token mix is, alongside training throughput to check that efficiency is preserved.
CONTROLS: Compare against load balancing alone, against a router orthogonality regulariser, and against the same loss with cluster labels permuted across tokens. Repeat every run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals for each metric.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: We expect sharper expert specialisation, a modest downstream gain and unchanged throughput. The result is weaker than hoped if the permuted-label run shows the same gain, since then the behaviour owes nothing to the clusters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-selective diversity penalty on expert outputs
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts (MoE) language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token, on 25 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text plus mathematics text. Apply a penalty on the similarity of expert outputs only in the middle third of the layers, where feed-forward network (FFN) representations are most transferable, with weight 0.02. Evaluate perplexity per source and accuracy on the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark, a grade-school mathematics set and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare against load balancing alone, against the penalty applied at every layer, and against the penalty in the first third of the layers only. Run three seeds each and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Applying the penalty in the middle layers should give the largest overlap reduction per unit of lost perplexity. If the all-layer version matches it, layer choice does not matter and the cheaper placement offers no advantage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-conflict regularisation between experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 30 billion tokens of English, Chinese and mathematics text. Estimate on each step the cosine between the gradients that two experts receive from the same batch, and penalize large positive values so that experts update in distinct directions, with weight 0.005. Evaluate held-out perplexity, GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and compute pairwise parameter-space distance between experts at the end of training.
CONTROLS: Compare with load balancing alone and with a weight-decay-only version that has the same parameter norm. Include a run that applies the penalty to random expert pairs, and repeat everything with three seeds.
COST: 850
PREDICTION: Experts should move apart in parameter space and downstream accuracy should rise slightly over load balancing alone. The penalty fails if it only slows training, shown by a higher perplexity with no accuracy gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy annealing of the router with a specialisation reward
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 32 experts per layer and top-two routing on 60 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematics text. Start with a high router temperature, lower it over the first tenth of training, and add a reward that grows when an expert's recent tokens share a topic label computed by a frozen small model. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare with load balancing alone, with the temperature schedule but no reward, and with the reward but a constant temperature. Run three seeds per configuration and report paired bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Expert overlap should fall and downstream accuracy should improve by about one point over load balancing alone. The reward could add nothing beyond the temperature schedule, which the temperature-only comparison will show.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cluster-first warm start for expert assignment
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 20 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. For the first five percent of training, we send tokens from each of 16 clusters of a small frozen model's representations to a fixed pair of experts, and then release the router and keep a mild cosine penalty on expert outputs. We evaluate perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: We compare with load balancing alone, with the warm start but no later penalty, and with a warm start using randomly assigned expert pairs. We repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: We expect lower overlap and a small gain on downstream scores relative to load balancing alone. We would doubt the idea if the randomly assigned warm start reaches the same overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Second-choice expert contrast loss
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 24 experts per layer and top-two routing on 40 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematics text. At each token, require the output of the top-ranked expert and that of the second-ranked expert to differ by at least a fixed distance in representation space, with weight 0.01, so that every chosen pair brings distinct functions. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare with load balancing alone, with a contrast loss on random expert pairs instead of ranked pairs, and with a router orthogonality regularizer. Run three seeds per configuration and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 770
PREDICTION: Overlap between co-selected experts should fall and downstream accuracy should rise a little above the load-balancing-only run. The loss helps little if the random-pair version reaches the same overlap, since ranked pairs then carry no extra signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-band specialisation targets for routed experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 30 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Bucket tokens by corpus frequency into four bands and add a loss that moves the average router distribution of each band toward a distinct group of four experts, with weight 0.02 and a linear decay to zero. Evaluate perplexity on frequent and rare token subsets, GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare with load balancing alone, with bands formed from randomly assigned tokens, and with a version that assigns experts to bands without the decay. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Rare-token perplexity should improve and overlap should fall relative to load balancing alone. Frequency bands may be a poor axis for functional specialisation, in which case downstream accuracy stays flat.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-expert subspace separation of input projections
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 8 experts per layer and two active per token on 15 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Add a penalty on the overlap between the dominant input subspaces of the first projection matrices of different experts, measured every hundred steps by a truncated singular value decomposition with weight 0.01. Evaluate held-out perplexity, GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare with load balancing alone, with a penalty on the output projections only, and with the same penalty on randomly paired layers. Run three seeds per configuration and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Subspace overlap should drop and downstream scores should rise a little. The penalty could cost perplexity at this small scale, which would show in the language modeling curve first.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Routed-output diversity loss added to the language modeling objective
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer, two active per token and 700 million active parameters on 30 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Add a term to the language modeling loss that lowers the cosine similarity between the mean outputs of different experts on the tokens routed to them, scaled by a coefficient of 0.01. Evaluate held-out perplexity in both languages, then GSM8K, C-Eval, MMLU and a reading comprehension suite, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same architecture trained with the load-balancing loss alone, on the same token stream and learning rate schedule. Compare against a version with global-batch load balancing, same data order. Compare against a router orthogonality regularizer, same coefficient range. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Expert overlap should drop and downstream accuracy should rise by about one point over the load-balancing-only run, with perplexity unchanged. The idea is refuted if overlap falls while accuracy stays within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity-regularized sparse pretraining against a dense counterpart
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a sparse language model with 8 experts per layer, two active per token and 700 million active parameters on a 30 billion token mix of English and Chinese web pages. Include a loss term that pushes apart the outputs of experts that see the same routed tokens, with cosine similarity as the distance and a coefficient of 0.05. Track held-out perplexity per language, accuracy on GSM8K, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and an expert overlap score computed on a validation mix with domain labels.
CONTROLS: Compare against a dense model with the same active parameter count, on the same token stream and learning rate schedule. Compare against a version with a larger global batch, same data order. Compare against an upcycled dense checkpoint, same coefficient range. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Overlap should drop and downstream accuracy should come within about one point of the dense model, with perplexity unchanged. The idea is refuted if overlap falls while accuracy stays within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cluster-assigned routing targets for expert specialization
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 32 experts per layer, two active per token and 1.2 billion active parameters on 60 billion tokens covering English pages, Chinese pages, mathematics text and encyclopedia text. Group token representations from a small reference model into 32 clusters, then add a loss of weight 0.02 that pulls each cluster toward a preferred pair of experts. Report perplexity per source, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and the share of each expert's tokens that comes from its top source.
CONTROLS: Repeat the run with the pull weight set to zero, same router and same data order. Run the pull weight at a low, a middle and a high value on a shorter schedule. Compare against a version where the cluster labels are permuted across tokens, same pull weight. Repeat each configuration with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Concentration per expert should rise and downstream scores should improve a little over the zero-weight run. Failure looks like permuted labels producing the same concentration, meaning the clusters carry little structure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenizer vocabulary and head count in a sparse model with cluster targets
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a sparse language model using 64 experts per layer, two active per token and 1.2 billion active parameters, on an English, Chinese, mathematics and encyclopedia mix of 60 billion tokens. Fit 32 groups to token representations from a small reference model and attach a loss term of weight 0.03 sending each group toward a chosen pair of experts. Score perplexity for each source, accuracy on GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and the fraction of each expert's tokens contributed by its leading source.
CONTROLS: Repeat the run with the tokenizer vocabulary enlarged, same router and same data order. Run the attention head count at a low, a middle and a high value on a shorter schedule. Compare against a version where the document order is permuted within each source, same pull weight. Repeat each configuration with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Concentration should rise and downstream scores should improve a little as the vocabulary grows. Failure looks like the head count shifting concentration as much as the vocabulary, meaning the routing targets matter little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mid-layer specialization loss on a multi-domain pretraining mix
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 12 layers, 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 20 billion tokens that mix English, Chinese, mathematics and encyclopedia text. Apply a mutual-information loss between the expert chosen at layers 4 to 9 and a coarse domain label taken from each document's source, with weight 0.03. Evaluate perplexity per domain, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and a reading comprehension suite, and measure the fraction of each domain's tokens that reaches its top three experts.
CONTROLS: Compare against the load-balancing loss alone, trained from scratch on the full multi-domain mix with the same schedule. Compare against the same term with domain labels reassigned across documents, same weight. Compare every run on held-out text from each of the four domains. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Domain concentration should rise at the middle layers and accuracy should improve by a point or so. The method stops looking useful if reassigned labels give the same concentration, as then the labels steer very little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router-guidance loss during short continued training of a converged checkpoint
PROPOSAL: Continue training a converged sparse language model with 12 layers, 16 experts per layer and two active per token for a short stage on 0.4 billion tokens of English instruction-style text. Attach a mutual-information term linking the expert picked at layers 4 to 9 with a coarse task label drawn from each example's type, weight 0.03. Measure perplexity on held-out instructions, accuracy on MMLU and a reading comprehension suite, and the fraction of each task type's tokens reaching its top three experts.
CONTROLS: Compare against the load-balancing loss alone, continued from the same converged checkpoint with the same schedule. Compare against the same term with task labels reassigned across examples, same weight. Compare every run on held-out text from the one instruction mix. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Task concentration should rise slightly and accuracy should move by a point or so. The method stops looking useful if reassigned labels give the same concentration, as then the labels steer very little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Source-entropy reward for expert specialization
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 24 layers, 64 experts per layer and 6 active per token on 100 billion tokens of English web text, Chinese web text and mathematics text. Add a loss that rewards each expert for concentrating on a distinct token mix, using the entropy of the expert's source distribution, with weight 0.01. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and score pairwise overlap of expert usage on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare downstream accuracy against the load-balancing-only run, same tokens and schedule. Compare pairwise expert overlap on the labelled validation mix against the same run. Compare perplexity per source against the same run, same data order. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall and accuracy should rise by about a point, with perplexity per source close to the reference run. The reward is refuted if overlap falls but accuracy stays within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router entropy and load spread under an entropy-based expert reward
PROPOSAL: Train a mixture of experts model with 20 layers, 64 experts per layer and 6 active per token on 100 billion tokens of English web text, Chinese web text and code-free mathematics text. Add a reward on the entropy of each expert's source distribution, scaled by 0.02, and log training loss, router entropy and the spread of expert load throughout the run, then compare final values on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare training loss against the load-balancing-only run, same tokens and schedule. Compare the spread of expert load on the labelled validation mix against the same run. Compare router entropy against the same run, same data order. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Router entropy and load spread should shift in the expected direction, with training loss close to the reference run. The reward is refuted if the statistics stay within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Targeted expert guidance loss at larger scale
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts model with 28 layers, 64 experts per layer and 4 active per token, using 2.5 billion active parameters and 200 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text, mathematics text and encyclopedia text. Add a loss that assigns each document source a preferred set of 8 experts and pulls the routing distribution toward it, with weight 0.02. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and score expert overlap on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare against the load-balancing loss alone, same tokens and schedule. Compare against a version of the same loss with the preferred expert sets permuted across sources, same weight. Compare against global-batch load balancing, same data order. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall and downstream accuracy should improve by a point or two. The guidance is shown to be unhelpful if the permuted-set run reaches the same accuracy as the correctly assigned one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Source-preference routing loss with a longer training stage
PROPOSAL: Build a sparse language model with 28 layers, 64 experts per layer and 4 active per token, using 2.5 billion active parameters, trained on a 200 billion token stream of web pages in two languages, mathematics text and encyclopedia entries. Give every document source a preferred group of 8 experts and attach a routing loss of weight 0.02 toward that group. Measure source-level perplexity, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, plus an overlap score for experts computed on a labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare against the load-balancing loss alone, same tokens and schedule. Compare against a version of the same loss with the router initialized differently, same weight. Compare against global-batch load balancing, same data order. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall and downstream accuracy should improve by a point or two. The preference loss is shown to be unhelpful if the differently initialized run reaches the same accuracy as the first one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-output decorrelation loss for specialization from the start of pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 40 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text. Add to the language modeling loss a term that penalizes cosine similarity between expert outputs on commonly routed tokens, with weight 0.01. Evaluate perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval, MMLU and reading comprehension accuracy against load balancing alone, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Compare against load balancing alone and against global-batch load balancing on the same stream. Include a router orthogonality regularizer and a permuted-pair version of the new loss. Repeat each run with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall and accuracy should rise by a point over load balancing alone, with perplexity unchanged. The approach is in doubt if the permuted-pair loss performs the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Merging overlapping experts of a trained model to measure homogenization
PROPOSAL: Take a trained mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token, pretrained on English and Chinese web text. Merge pairs of experts by averaging weights after clustering them by output similarity on a held-out domain mix, and measure the change in perplexity, GSM8K, C-Eval, MMLU and reading comprehension accuracy as the number of merged pairs grows from 1 to 8 on 2000 held-out documents. Treat the damage per merge as a measure of how overlapping experts are.
CONTROLS: Compare against merging randomly chosen pairs and against dropping the same experts outright. Include a merge of the pairs with the highest weight cosine. Repeat the clustering with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Similar experts should merge with small loss and random pairs with larger loss. The measure is uninformative if random and similar pairs cost the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining a mixture of experts with a router-guidance loss versus load balancing
PROPOSAL: Pretrain two mixture of experts language models with 8 experts per layer and two active per token on 12 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematics text, one with a mutual-information loss between the chosen expert and a token cluster identity, weight 0.02, and one with load balancing alone. Compare held-out perplexity, GSM8K, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Add a run with the cluster identity permuted across tokens, and a run with global-batch load balancing. Repeat all runs with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals for every metric.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The guided model should show lower overlap and a gain of about a point on downstream scores. The loss is no better than chance structure if the permuted run matches it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continued training of a converged sparse model under a routing-guidance term
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a converged sparse language model having 8 experts per layer and two active per token for a short stage on 0.5 billion tokens of English instruction and mathematics text, adding a mutual-information term between the chosen expert and a token cluster identity, weight 0.02, in one arm and load balancing alone in the other. Contrast held-out perplexity, GSM8K and reading comprehension accuracy, and measure an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix.
CONTROLS: Add a run with the cluster identity permuted across tokens, and a run with global-batch load balancing. Repeat all runs with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals for every metric.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Overlap should change little and downstream scores should move by a fraction of a point. The loss is no better than chance structure if the permuted run matches it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sequence-level domain targets for expert assignment
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 32 experts per layer and top-two routing on 80 billion tokens of English web text, Chinese web text, mathematics text and encyclopedia text. Add an auxiliary loss that lifts the probability of a small expert subset for each document source and lowers it for the other experts, with weight 0.02. Evaluate perplexity per source, GSM8K, C-Eval and MMLU accuracy, and measure how concentrated each expert's tokens are by source.
CONTROLS: Compare against load balancing alone and against the same loss with source labels permuted across documents. Include a global-batch load-balancing run, and repeat each with three seeds, reporting bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Concentration should rise and downstream scores should improve by a point, with perplexity per source close to the load-balancing run. The idea is in doubt if permuted labels give the same gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capacity factor and router temperature tuning for MoE throughput
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 32 experts per layer and top-two routing on 80 billion tokens of English web text, Chinese web text, mathematics text and encyclopedia text. Tune the capacity factor and the router temperature to reach the highest tokens per second without dropping tokens, then confirm held-out perplexity per source, GSM8K, C-Eval and MMLU accuracy at the chosen settings, and measure how evenly experts are loaded.
CONTROLS: Compare against the default capacity factor and temperature, and against a configuration with a larger capacity factor. Include a global-batch load-balancing run, and repeat each with three seeds, reporting bootstrap intervals.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Throughput should rise a few percent with accuracy unchanged. The tuning is in doubt if throughput gains vanish across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Specialization loss compared across two scales of mixture of experts pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain mixture of experts language models with a diversity loss on expert outputs, weight 0.02, at 400 million and 1.6 billion active parameters, each on 35 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematics text, each with 16 experts per layer and two active per token. Evaluate perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and MMLU accuracy, and compute an expert overlap score on a domain-labelled validation mix, to see whether the effect of the loss grows with scale.
CONTROLS: Compare each scale against load balancing alone on the same stream and against a router orthogonality regularizer. Repeat all runs with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall at both scales and the accuracy gain should grow with size. The trend is not supported if the gain at the larger scale is not above the smaller one by more than seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity loss on feed-forward unit groups of a dense transformer
PROPOSAL: Pretrain dense transformer language models having a diversity loss on groups of feed-forward units, weight 0.02, at 400 million and 1.6 billion parameters, on 35 billion tokens of Chinese and English web pages plus mathematics text, splitting each feed-forward layer into 16 groups. Evaluate perplexity per language, GSM8K and MMLU accuracy, and compute a group overlap score on a validation mix with domain labels, to see whether the effect of the loss grows with scale.
CONTROLS: Compare each scale against the same dense model without the loss and against a weight orthogonality regularizer. Repeat all runs with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall at both scales and the accuracy gain should grow with size. The trend is not supported if the gain at the larger scale is not above the smaller one by more than seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-wise routing statistics and downstream results under a guidance loss
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token on 30 billion tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematics text, adding a loss of weight 0.02 that pulls the routing of each document source toward a preferred expert subset. Measure the share of every source's tokens that reaches its subset on a labelled validation mix, together with perplexity per source, GSM8K, C-Eval and reading comprehension accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare against load balancing alone and against permuted source assignments, same weight. Include a global-batch load-balancing run, and repeat each with three seeds, reporting bootstrap intervals.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The share reaching the preferred subset should rise sharply and downstream accuracy should rise by about a point. The guidance fails if shares rise but accuracy does not.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Linear decoding of token identity from router logits of a trained model
PROPOSAL: Take a trained mixture of experts language model with 16 experts per layer and two active per token, pretrained on English and Chinese web text and mathematics text. Fit linear decoders that predict the identity of the current token and of its source from the router logits at layers 4, 8 and 12, and measure decoding accuracy for the most frequent 5000 tokens and for each of the three sources on a labelled validation mix, together with perplexity per source.
CONTROLS: Compare against decoders fitted on router logits of a randomly initialized model and against decoders on shuffled logits. Repeat the fitting with three seeds, reporting bootstrap intervals.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Decoding of token identity should far exceed chance in all layers and source decoding should be weaker. The probe is uninformative if random-model decoding matches the trained one.
